title: Bamies
subtitle: Greek braised okra in tomato sauce
excerpt: Okra braised slowly in a tomato and olive oil sauce with onion and garlic. A simple Greek side dish that pairs well with bread, feta and grilled meat.
sourceNotes: Traditional Greek vegetable dish, particularly common in summer. Synthesised from multiple Greek home cook sources.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions. Reheat gently on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use a wider pan so the okra sits in a single layer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes better the next day. Make ahead and reheat gently.

content.text: Bamies is okra cooked low and slow in olive oil and tomato. The key is not to stir it once it starts simmering. Moving the okra breaks the pods and makes the sauce sticky rather than silky.

items.prepNote: tops trimmed to a cone shape, not cut into the pod
one tin, crushed with your hands

content.text: Trim the tops of the okra into a cone shape. Do not cut into the flesh or it will release the sticky sap. Rinse and dry well.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for 10 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes, vinegar and sugar. Season with salt and pepper. Stir and simmer for 5 minutes.
Lay the okra in the sauce in a single layer. Do not stir. Spoon a little sauce over the top.
Cover and cook on a low heat for 35 to 40 minutes. Shake the pan gently once or twice but do not stir.
Scatter over the parsley and serve warm or at room temperature with crusty bread.

items.cause: The okra pods were cut into, or they were stirred during cooking.
items.fix: Always trim in a cone shape above the flesh. Shake the pan rather than stirring once the okra goes in.
Check the okra at 30 minutes. It should be tender but still hold its shape. Remove from heat as soon as a knife goes through easily.
Add an extra pinch of sugar and cook for 5 more minutes. A good drizzle of fresh olive oil at the end also helps.
